summary: Iteration 10 — frontend-only verification of WA bug fixes A (group-only phone-number sender label on message bubbles) & B (JID normalization for two-way chat sync). Pod has no real Baileys socket so chat/message rendering verified via (1) code review of /app/frontend/src/pages/WhatsApp.jsx + /app/wa-service/src/sessionManager.js + /app/wa-service/src/index.js and (2) Playwright execution of the actual exported helper functions (formatPhone, jidName) in the browser context against representative JID inputs. Regression checks performed for Settings, LinkedIn Prospect tabs, and /whatsapp empty state.

bug_fix_A_message_bubble_sender_label.evidence: WhatsApp.jsx lines 644-648: sender label rendered ONLY when `!m.from_me && activeJid?.includes('@g.us') && m.sender_jid`. Uses `formatPhone(m.sender_jid)` (not push_name). Wrapped in `font-mono` and `data-testid=wa-msg-sender-{message_id}`. Private chats receive NO sender label above bubble (condition fails). Group chats render the normalized phone number (e.g. `+6281234567890`). Cannot exercise runtime path: pod has 0 connected accounts (empty state shown).

bug_fix_B_jid_normalization.evidence: sessionManager.js line 9 imports `jidNormalizedUser`; lines 357-362 export `normJid()` helper (skips @g.us/@broadcast, falls back on error). `persistMessage` (line 368) normalizes both wa_messages.jid and wa_chats.jid via normJid. `chats.upsert` (203), `chats.update` (228), `contacts.upsert` (243) all normalize. `sendText` (436) and `sendMedia` (445) normalize target JID before `sock.sendMessage`. index.js line 11 imports `normJid`; messages GET endpoint (lines 137-141) uses `$in: [normalized, raw]` for backward compat with legacy rows.

chat_list_phone_primary.evidence: WhatsApp.jsx line 565 uses font-mono + data-testid=wa-chat-name-{jid} rendering `jidName(c.jid, c.name)`. Lines 574-578 render italic secondary alias with data-testid=wa-chat-alias-{jid}, prefixed with `~`, only for non-group chats with c.name set.

chat_header.evidence: WhatsApp.jsx line 613: header div uses font-mono + data-testid=wa-active-header showing `jidName(activeJid)`. Lines 614-620 render italic `~alias` secondary line for private chats where alias exists.

regression_checks.whatsapp_page_loads: PASS — /whatsapp shows empty state 'Belum ada akun WhatsApp' with Add WhatsApp button visible (data-testid=wa-add-account count=1). No console errors.
regression_checks.settings_target_harian: PASS — Settings page renders with sidebar tabs: Companies, Users, Roles, Target Harian, Working Days, Categories, Locations, Hunter.io API. Did NOT click into Target Harian tab to confirm Email/LinkedIn split panels rendered (basic regression only).
regression_checks.linkedin_prospect_tabs: PASS — /linkedin renders all 5 tabs found in DOM: 1·Jadwal, 2·Add Prospect (1/20), 3·Connect, 4·Analitik, Prospect List. Pipeline distribution chart + filter UI working.
regression_checks.scrapingdog_search: NOT TESTED — would require business action; out of scope for bug verification scope.

critical_code_review_comments: normJid() in sessionManager.js correctly falls back to raw JID when jidNormalizedUser throws, and short-circuits for @g.us/@broadcast — sound design.
GET messages endpoint uses $in:[normalized, raw] only when normalized != raw — efficient, avoids unnecessary index scan.

Minor: persistMessage uses upsert key `{session_id, message_id, jid}`. If a single message_id arrives once with raw JID (legacy) and again with normalized JID (post-fix), MongoDB unique index `{session_id:1, message_id:1, jid:1}` could create a duplicate row. Risk is bounded (only during the transition window), but worth noting for migration.

Sender label in group chats relies on `m.sender_jid` which is set in persistMessage from `msg.key.participant`. For Baileys, this is correct — participant is the actual sender's JID in groups, distinct from chat JID. Good.
Frontend `jidName` deliberately discards alias for private chats — per product requirement (push_name is set by the OTHER user and untrustworthy). Comment in lines 23-25 documents intent clearly.

seed_data_creation: None. Pod has no Baileys WA socket so no chat/message rows can be created. All helper logic verified by executing the same JS in browser context against synthetic JID inputs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fixes A & B are code-verified. To do a live end-to-end test you would need: (1) a real WhatsApp account scanned via QR on a host that can reach WA servers (pod cannot), (2) two devices to exchange messages and confirm: same canonical JID in wa_messages docs for inbound + outbound, and (3) a group chat to confirm the wa-msg-sender-{id} label shows + the sender phone (not push_name). All helper math + selectors are correct per static review.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration was a verification pass for fixes already merged. No new bug RCA needed. Original RCA (per request): outbound messages were being stored with un-normalized JID (e.g. `62812...@s.whatsapp.net`) while inbound from the same contact sometimes arrived with device suffix (`62812...:12@s.whatsapp.net`) or LID form, causing them to land in different wa_chats rows. Mitigation: normalize every JID at every write site (persistMessage, chats.upsert/update, contacts.upsert) and every send (sendText, sendMedia). Read site (GET messages) tolerates legacy raw JIDs via $in lookup.
